# Featured openings

The next era of veterinary oncology starts here

At the University of Minnesota we are investing in people, programs, and partnerships to build a premier destination for veterinary oncology.

Our vision combines exceptional clinical care, groundbreaking research, and outstanding training within a uniquely integrated cancer ecosystem. As one of the few veterinary  programs directly connected to an NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center, we bring together veterinary medicine, human medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, engineering, and the health sciences to advance cancer care and discovery.

## UMN employee benefits

The University of Minnesota offers top-tier benefits for employees, including: 

  * Excellent, low-cost medical and dental insurance
  * 12 paid holidays and 22 paid vacation days per year
  * Automatic retirement plan with 10% employer contribution and 5.5% employee contribution
  * Additional voluntary retirement plans to help you save even more for retirement

## Today

Established specialty oncology services, collaborative patient care, a strong commitment to resident education, outstanding facilities and equipment (Varian Edge, 3T MR, dual source CT with gating, interventional suite and Medtronic StealthStation S8), a supportive referring community, a well-honed clinical trial infrastructure, and productive long-standing supportive relationships with colleagues throughout other colleges in the Health Sciences interested in comparative oncology.

## Growing

Significant investment in oncology expansion, including five new faculty positions and the development of an additional endowed chair to support long-term excellence and innovation. This planned growth complements growth throughout the College and Veterinary Medical Center with new leadership and many new faculty in medical imaging, surgery, neurology, ophthalmology, anesthesia, and other specialties

## Tomorrow

A leading destination for comparative oncology, where clinical excellence and translational discovery intersect. Opportunities include collaboration across the health sciences and engagement in cuing-edge research spanning immunotherapy, precision medicine, early detection, and clinical trials.

# Medical Oncology and Radiation Therapy

Cancer in pets is relatively common and one of the leading causes of death. There are many different types of cancer and many treatments available. Our goals upon consulting with you are

  * to provide information about your pet’s condition, the treatment options available, and likely outcomes,
  * to respect and support family choices, and
  * most importantly, to maximize the quality of life of the pet.

We look forward to welcoming clients and pets back to our radiation therapy service!

What to expect

#### 

The Clinical Oncology Team

Just as in human medicine, veterinary specialists are available to help general practitioners with complex cases. Veterinary specialists are individuals who have spent several years in intense training studying their disciplines and undergo rigorous examinations to ensure they meet the qualifications of a specialist. The Oncology Service provides integrated oncology care with colleagues in soft tissue surgery, oncologic surgery, pathology, medical oncology, and radiation therapy who work to provide comprehensive care for referral cases. Adopting this integrated approach allows us to provide thoughtful approaches to oncology cases that may benefit from multi-modality therapy with surgery, radiation therapy and/or chemotherapy. The oncology team is composed of board-certified specialists in medical oncology, radiation oncology, oncologic and soft tissue surgery, interns and residents in the midst of intense specialty training, and dedicated teams of veterinary nurses who strive to provide outstanding patient care. 
Resources

#### 

Comparative Oncology

The University of Minnesota is home to the Animal Cancer Care and Research (ACCR) Program, which supports the clinical oncology service, but also strives to determine the underlying causes for malignancies and identify similarities and differences between cancers in animals and humans. This allows us to develop new diagnostic and treatment strategies that may be helpful across species.

#### 

Clinical trials

Clinical trials are an important means by which we learn more about cancer and potential new treatments. Participation in trials may help reduce some of the costs associated with cancer treatment.

Learn more about the Oncology clinical trials offered by the College of Veterinary Medicine

#### 

Client handouts

We are currently working to include many different client handouts on our website. Some clients wish to see some general information ahead of their appointment but this can also serve as a reference after an appointment. Please note that these are general information guides and not all information is applicable to your pet.  This is a work in progress so please bear with us as we provide comprehensive materials.

# Advanced Veterinary Oncology in Oakdale, MN

We know how stressful it can be when your pet develops unusual symptoms or doesn’t seem like themselves. At Animal Emergency & Referral Center of Minnesota (AERC), our veterinary oncology team is here to help. With specialized training and expertise in diagnosing and treating many types of cancer, we work with you to create a treatment plan focused on both effective care and quality of life.

Our promise is to provide unparalleled treatment and support every step of the way.

## Understanding Cancer and Exploring Treatment Options

We offer consultations and chemotherapy treatments to support pets and their families through a difficult time. By arranging a consultation through your primary veterinarian, our team can carefully evaluate your pet’s condition and discuss the treatment options available.

## Pet Cancer Services at AERC

### Advanced Diagnostics

Because pets can’t tell us what’s wrong, we use state-of-the-art diagnostic tools to understand their condition and determine the best treatment options. Advanced surgical techniques help reduce complications and support faster recovery.

### Radiation

While AERC does not provide radiation therapy on-site, we partner with trusted facilities in the Midwest to coordinate treatment and guide pet parents through the referral process.

### Advanced Imaging

Our oncology team works closely with radiology for cancer diagnosis, staging, and treatment monitoring. Imaging, such as CT scans or X-rays, allows us to track tumor growth, evaluate treatment effectiveness, and plan next steps.

### Immunotherapy

Currently, immunotherapy for pets is limited to a vaccine for dogs with oral melanoma. This treatment trains the immune system to fight cancer cells and can be combined with other therapies. Research continues to expand future options.

### Hospice and Palliative Care

Oncology isn’t solely about treatment—it’s also about comfort. Our team provides palliative care to ease pain, improve quality of life, and support families, whether or not active cancer treatments are being pursued.

### End-of-Life Care

If the tough days start to outweigh the good ones, our team offers peaceful and compassionate euthanasia services or referral to in-home providers. Our Pet Loss Support page is here to help—offering tools, group support, and caring advice to comfort you.

## How to Make An Appointment

Oncology services are available at our Oakdale location.

  * Pet Owner Appointments
If your pet has been diagnosed with cancer or you’re concerned about symptoms, we’re here to help. To learn more about oncology services or discuss treatment options, contact the team by phone, email (info@aercmn.com), or through our online form.
  * Veterinarian Referrals
Veterinarians, please send referrals using the online form, email (info@aercmn.com), or by calling, with patient history included for context.

Request an Appointment

# Dr. Wolf-Ringwall

### DVM, PhD, DACVIM (Oncology)

Board Certified Veterinary Medical Oncologist

Oncology

Dr. Amber Wolf-Ringwall is a board-certified veterinary medical oncologist. She attended Colorado State University (CSU) where she received her BS and PhD degrees in Biomedical Sciences. Dr. Wolf developed a passion for veterinary oncology and cancer research when her two young dogs developed lymphoma during her PhD training, which led her to pursue veterinary school. She received her veterinary degree from CSU in 2014 and completed a one-year rotating internship at North Carolina State University. She then completed a 3-year medical oncology residency at the CSU Flint Animal Cancer Center.

Dr. Wolf moved to Minnesota in 2018 to join the oncology team at the University of Minnesota. She served as a clinical assistant professor, enjoying roles in teaching, research, and leadership as the section head of the clinical oncology service. In 2023, Dr. Wolf explored various locum opportunities around the country in both academia and private practice to broaden her perspective and gain real-world experience. She then had the honor of joining the Red River Animal Emergency Hospital & Referral Center in Fargo to establish the first veterinary oncology practice for pets in her home state of North Dakota.

Dr. Wolf has a special interest in hematologic cancers such as lymphoma/leukemia, cytology and molecular diagnostic tests, clinical trials, comparative oncology, and in helping families navigate their pet’s cancer journey. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her husband and their dogs Violet and Sisu, hiking and enjoying nature, traveling, cheering on the Denver Broncos, watching Formula 1 races, attending concerts, and exploring the Twin Cities with family and friends.
